newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia coal strike may hit exports-Arco.
newsitem.headline: Australia coal strike may hit exports-Arco.

text.p: A strike at United States energy giant Atlantic Richfield Co's (Arco) Curragh coal mine in central Queensland could soon affect exports as stockpiles diminish, a Curragh coal official said.

"We've now lost the best part of two months' production and we seem to be no closer to resolving this dispute," Bruce Denney, managing director of Curragh Queensland Mining Ltd said in a statement on Tuesday.
The dispute at the Curragh mine started in April and centred on negotiations on rosters and redundancies during talks on a new wage agreement with trade unions.
Denney told Reuters production of thermal and coking coal which totalled five million tonnes last year, were being lost at the rate of 100,000 tonnes a week.
Exports through the eastern coast port of Gladstone were for customers in India, Japan and Europe, Denney said.
He said the effect of the strike on exports would soon start to be felt as stockpiles held at Gladstone started to run down.

Denney said the dispute, which had now gone to the Federal Court, was not connected with the decision by Arco in April to sell its Australian coal assets, comprising the Curragh, Gordonstone and Blair Athol mines.
Arco said at the time of its announcement that offers for the three mines would be examined but a sale or float of the assets could take up to a year to complete.
Arco said it was quitting its global coal assets to focus more clearly on oil, gas and specialty chemicals.
